record.paper_title: Lower Bounds for Unrestricted Boolean Circuits: Open Problems
record.original_question: Can gate elimination alone be used to prove a 4n lower bound on the number of gates needed to compute some n-input Boolean function by a Boolean circuit?

evidence.quote: Can one at least prove a 4n lower bound using gate elimination?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Boolean circuit over the full binary basis B_2 (the set of all Boolean functions {0,1}^2 → {0,1}) is a directed acyclic graph whose sources are labeled by input variables x_1, …, x_n or constants, whose internal nodes (gates) have fan-in 2 and are labeled by functions in B_2, and which has a designated output node; the size of the circuit is the number of gates. The "gate elimination" method is the standard inductive technique for proving circuit-size lower bounds: one identifies a small set of input variables whose restriction (substituting constants 0/1) is guaranteed to eliminate at least k gates from any optimal circuit for the function, yielding by induction a lower bound of the form k·n − O(1) on the circuit size of an explicit family of Boolean functions f_n : {0,1}^n → {0,1}.

Question: Does there exist an explicit family of Boolean functions f_n : {0,1}^n → {0,1} for which a pure gate-elimination argument can prove that every B_2-circuit computing f_n has size at least 4n − O(1)?
artifact.category_tag: Boolean circuit lower bounds via gate elimination
artifact.status_search_result: Lower bounds of 4n−O(1), 4.5n−o(n) (Lachish–Raz), and 5n−o(n) (Iwama–Morizumi) have been proved using gate-elimination style arguments, but these are over the U_2 basis (B_2 minus parity/its negation), not the full binary basis B_2 considered here. Over B_2 the best known bound is 3.1n−o(n) (Li–Yang, STOC 2022), and works such as "On the Limits of Gate Elimination" (Golovnev et al., MFCS 2016) explicitly establish barriers for the gate-elimination technique over B_2. Whether a 4n lower bound over B_2 is achievable via pure gate elimination appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: 3.1n − o(n) circuit lower bounds for explicit functions
status_evidence.snippet: 3.1n − o(n) circuit lower bounds over the full binary basis B_2.
status_evidence.claim: The current best B_2 lower bound is 3.1n−o(n), well below 4n.

status_evidence.title: On the Limits of Gate Elimination
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes limitations of the gate-elimination technique for circuit lower bounds.
status_evidence.claim: Known barriers exist for gate-elimination arguments over B_2.

status_evidence.title: An Explicit Lower Bound of 5n − o(n) for Boolean Circuits
status_evidence.snippet: 5n−o(n) lower bound via gate elimination over the U_2 basis.
status_evidence.claim: Over U_2, gate elimination yields bounds exceeding 4n, but B_2 is different.
